title: Blockbuster Turned Down a $50 Million Deal. Then Netflix Won
description:
In 2000, Netflix's founders flew to Dallas and offered to sell their company to Blockbuster for $50 million. Blockbuster said no. Ten years later it was bankrupt. The full rise-and-fall story: late fees, debt, a boardroom fight, and one last store in Bend, Oregon.

Dramatised: scenes are illustrations; the facts come from the sources below. The reaction in the meeting is Netflix's account.

Sources:
• Marketplace: CEO Reed Hastings on how Netflix beat Blockbuster
• Fortune: Netflix co-founder Marc Randolph recalls Blockbuster rejecting chance to buy it
• Newsweek fact-check: Did Blockbuster turn down a chance to buy Netflix for $50 million
• CNBC: How Netflix almost lost the movie rental wars to Blockbuster
• Home Media Magazine: Icahn, Antioco opine on Blockbuster's fall
• Oregon Encyclopedia: Last Blockbuster video store in the U.S.
• Business Insider: The rise and fall of Blockbuster
